landing.heroBody: flashkarte is a spaced-repetition flashcard app. Write your cards in plain Markdown — or let your own AI build them — and it schedules each review for the moment right before you'd forget. Study on the web or on Android, always in sync.
landing.feature1Body: Write cards in plain Markdown — paste, import a file, or generate them. No clunky editors.
landing.feature2Body: A proven SM-2 schedule shows you each card right before you'd forget it, so reviews stay short.
landing.feature3Body: Web and Android, in sync. Pick up your reviews on the bus and finish them at your desk.
landing.feature4Body: Connect your own AI assistant over MCP to turn notes into decks — no extra subscription.

privacy.title: flashkarte — Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: flashkarte is a Markdown-based flashcard app with spaced-repetition study, operated by Christopher Rehm (Germany). This policy explains what data the app collects, why, and your choices. Questions or requests: <0>car2187bus@pm.me</0>.
privacy.collectAccount: <0>Account details</0> — your email address and a password. The password is never stored in plain text; only a salted hash is kept.
privacy.collectContent: <0>Your content</0> — the flashcard decks and cards you create or import, and your study progress (review history and scheduling).
privacy.collectApiKeys: <0>API keys</0> — if you generate a key to connect an AI client via the MCP server, we store a hashed form of that key (shown to you in full only once).
privacy.collectDiagnostics: <0>Diagnostic reports</0> — when the app hits an error it may send a report (error message, technical stack trace, app version, and platform) to our server log so we can fix bugs. These reports are used only for debugging.
privacy.dontAds: No advertising, no ad networks, and no sale or rental of personal data.
privacy.dontSell: We do not sell or rent your personal data to anyone.
privacy.dontTrain: We do not use your decks or content to train any model.
privacy.aiBody: flashkarte lets you connect your own AI assistant (for example via Claude) through a hosted MCP server, using a personal API key, so the AI can create decks in your account. When you use that, requests are processed by <0>your own</0> AI provider under their terms and privacy policy — the AI computation does not run on our servers.
privacy.storageHeading: How your data is stored and protected
privacy.storageBody: Data is stored on privately managed IONOS servers in Frankfurt, Germany. All traffic is encrypted with HTTPS (TLS). Passwords and API keys are stored only as hashes. Encrypted database backups are retained for no more than three months.
privacy.retentionBody: We keep account data while your account exists. Application and mail logs, analytics data, and app bug reports are deleted after 90 days; audit records are deleted after 12 months; MCP refresh-token records are deleted after 30 days. You can delete individual decks in the app. To delete your account and associated data, email <0>car2187bus@pm.me</0> from your account email address. Backups expire within three months.
privacy.analyticsBody: With your consent, we use self-hosted Umami analytics to understand aggregate use of the service. The analytics script is not loaded until you accept, and analytics records are deleted after 90 days. You can change your choice at any time; a page reload is used to apply it.
privacy.recipientsBody: We process service data on our IONOS infrastructure in Frankfurt, Germany. If you submit an in-app bug report, it is stored in a private GitHub issue. When you connect an AI assistant through MCP, the content you choose to send is processed by that AI provider under its own terms and privacy policy.
privacy.childrenBody: flashkarte is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect data from them.
privacy.rightsBody: Depending on where you live, including under the EU GDPR, you may have rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability, and complaint to a supervisory authority. Contact us at the address above to exercise your rights.
privacy.changesBody: If this policy changes, we will update the date at the top of this page.

analyticsConsent.label: Analytics consent
analyticsConsent.body: We use optional, self-hosted analytics to improve flashkarte. Analytics data is deleted after 90 days.

gettingStarted.metaDescription: How to sign up and get studying with flashkarte.
gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.signupBody: Create an account with an email and password, then confirm the verification email flashkarte sends you. Your decks and study progress are tied to that account and sync across every device you sign in on — web and Android.
gettingStarted.loopBody: flashkarte has one core loop: write a deck, then study it. New cards appear as "New"; once you've reviewed a card, spaced repetition decides when it's next "due". Studying regularly, even briefly, is what makes the schedule work.
gettingStarted.mapDecks: My Decks — your decks, with due counts and quick actions to study, share, or delete.
gettingStarted.mapLibrary: Library — search public decks shared by other users and clone one into your account.
gettingStarted.mapExplore: Explore — browse public decks without signing in.
gettingStarted.mapSettings: Settings — account, appearance, language, AI connection, and data.

writingDecks.metaDescription: The Markdown format flashkarte uses for cards, and the three ways to create a deck.
writingDecks.title: Writing decks
writingDecks.waysHeading: Three ways to create a deck
writingDecks.waysWeb: On the web, open the deck editor, paste or type Markdown in the format below, and save. A live preview shows the parsed cards before you save.
writingDecks.waysAndroid: In the Android app, create or import a deck the same way, using the same Markdown format.
writingDecks.waysAI: Let an AI assistant build a deck for you — see Creating decks with AI.
writingDecks.formatIntro: A deck is plain Markdown. The first heading is the title; an optional italic line under it is decorative and ignored. Use second-level headings to group cards into categories.
writingDecks.formatCardsIntro: Write cards in either of two styles — you can mix both in one deck:
writingDecks.formatBold: Numbered bold front: a bold line like "**1. front**" starts a card; the lines below it are the answer.
writingDecks.formatQA: Q:/A: format: a "Q:" line is the front; the first "A:" line is the answer, and any lines after it become a second paragraph.
writingDecks.formatParagraphs: Within an answer, consecutive lines join into one paragraph; leave a blank line to start a new paragraph.
writingDecks.settingsOrdered: Study in order: cards are shown in their authored order, and you must answer the current card correctly before advancing — useful for sequences that build on each other.

branchingDecks.metaDescription: How to write a choose-your-path branching deck in flashkarte.
branchingDecks.title: Branching decks
branchingDecks.body: Turn a deck into a choose-your-path sequence instead of a plain review. Put an anchor like "[label]" on its own line before a card, then give each option as a line "- choice text -> target", where target is another anchor's label (or "end" to finish). A card with no options is a normal, dead-end card. Any deck with at least one option card automatically becomes a branching deck, played rather than reviewed.

studying.metaDescription: How SM-2 spaced repetition scheduling works, what the rating buttons do, and what the deck counters mean.
studying.title: Studying & spaced repetition
studying.srsBody: flashkarte schedules reviews with the SM-2 algorithm. Every card has a due date. Cards you rate highly move further into the future; cards you struggle with come back sooner — often the next day. The goal is to see each card right before you'd otherwise forget it, so review sessions stay short.
studying.ratingsIntro: After you reveal a card's answer, rate how well you recalled it. This is what schedules the next review — be honest, not optimistic.
studying.ratingAgain: Again — you didn't recall it. The card resets: it comes back tomorrow, and its next interval starts over from the beginning.
studying.ratingHard: Hard — you recalled it, but it was a struggle. The next interval grows, but by less than Good.
studying.ratingGood: Good — you recalled it correctly with reasonable effort. The interval grows at the normal pace.
studying.ratingEasy: Easy — recalling it felt effortless. The interval grows the most, and future intervals for this card grow faster too.
studying.countersHeading: What the numbers on a deck mean
studying.countersIntro: Each deck lists its cards by status:
studying.counterDue: Due — cards ready to study right now (new cards, plus reviewed cards whose scheduled date has arrived).
studying.counterNew: New — cards you haven't studied yet.
studying.counterViewed: Viewed — cards you've studied at least once.
studying.counterAgain: Again — cards whose most recent review was rated Again.
studying.counterHard: Hard — cards whose most recent review was rated Hard.
studying.counterGood: Good — cards whose most recent review was rated Good.
studying.counterEasy: Easy — cards whose most recent review was rated Easy.
studying.counterNote: Again/Hard/Good/Easy reflect only the latest review of each card, not a running total — so together they always add up to the Viewed count.
studying.choiceBody: The Android app also offers a multiple-choice mode, which builds answer options automatically from your other cards and grades you the moment you tap one.

ai.metaTitle: Creating decks with AI — flashkarte Help
ai.metaDescription: How to connect your own AI assistant to flashkarte over MCP to build decks for you.
ai.title: Creating decks with AI
ai.body: An AI assistant can build decks for you and push them straight into your account, using your own AI account — flashkarte's server never runs the AI itself.
ai.step1: In Settings, generate an API key and copy the MCP server URL.
ai.step2: Add the URL as a custom connector in your AI client (for example claude.ai or Claude Desktop) and sign in with your flashkarte account.
ai.step3: Ask it to build a deck, e.g. "Turn this into a flashkarte deck: …", and the new deck appears in your account, ready to study.

sharing.metaDescription: How to make a deck public, browse the Explore page, and clone decks from the Library.
sharing.title: Sharing & exploring
sharing.publicBody: Make one of your decks public from the My Decks page to get a shareable link and have it listed for others to find. You can unshare it again at any time. The answers stay hidden to visitors until they sign up to study it.
sharing.exploreBody: Explore lets anyone — signed in or not — browse and preview public decks shared by other flashkarte users.
sharing.libraryBody: Library is the signed-in version: search public decks and clone any of them straight into your own account to start studying immediately.

publicDeck.cta: Sign up free to reveal the answers and study this deck with spaced repetition.
